headline: US Job Openings Rise to Four-Month High in September
summary: U.S. job openings rose in September to a four-month high and hiring increased, signaling mild improvement in a sluggish labor market.
why: Employment data is a primary indicator monitored by the Federal Reserve and financial markets to gauge economic momentum and forecast future monetary policy decisions.

impacts.name: US 10-year Treasury yield
impacts.why: Stronger labor market data can reduce expectations for aggressive Federal Reserve rate cuts, pushing yields higher.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected job openings indicate persistent economic resilience, reducing pressure on the central bank to aggressively ease monetary policy.
